recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If future validation shows the current external kindling/validator publisher no longer enforces the cardinality derivation rule, track that as a tooling issue in the publisher/validator codebase rather than as a core spec source correction.
issue_request: FHIR-7800 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core profiling issue asking the publishing tools to warn when a derived profile uses cardinalities not allowed by the base definition, such as changing a base 0..1 element to 0..*.
initial_application: The Jira application comment says "svn revision 5954 - add warnings." Git history contains that SVN import as commit f50c21837c0d37e53da00f4d29fd0594d3c5f24e, "#7800 - detect illegal cardinalities in profiles," which added min/max derivation warning checks to the old tools/java ProfileUtilities implementation.
additional_context: The current profiling page says profiles can restrict cardinality only within the limits of the base structure and includes a base-vs-derived cardinality table showing which cardinality changes are allowed. The current Gradle build runs the external org.hl7.fhir:kindling publisher artifact, and the historical tools/java tree changed by r5954 is absent. Related FHIR-7799 added the cardinality documentation table, while adjacent FHIR-7801 and FHIR-7802 audit commits already cover the neighboring binding-strength documentation and tooling-warning issues.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Editing current core source would either duplicate existing profiling prose or target obsolete/absent tooling files rather than the current publisher implementation.
